documents.reason: Both versions use the manufacturer's title and count to distinguish similar boxes and invite contributors to describe image-specific difficulty. Takers still decide about playable incomplete puzzles from a removable gap marker. Turning large sections over still eases disassembly, and the last builder is invited to separate pieces before donating. Actual piece sizes and sample outlines help people compare sets, while a child's reach explains the bottom-shelf placement and visible age guidance. A donor image is called for when a damaged lid needs a substitute, and donors are asked to take back damp or mildewed boxes because neighboring boxes can spoil. The box identifier still enables reports after a title is forgotten, matching pieces kept in labeled envelopes behind the desk, and locating a puzzle from a builder's photo. Volunteers still tally both directions at every opening and use the trend to time the next donation window.
